A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Calibration Tokens study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v5 retains the earlier supplementary material and adds Appendix C; pagination changes do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: v4 reports original depth-estimation experiments on ScanNet++ and KITTI-360, including baseline comparisons, finetuning experiments, and ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including quantitative comparisons and supplementary qualitative and ablation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same layer-wise Calibration Tokens, frozen encoder/decoder weights, synthetic fisheye generation, and inverse-warped self-supervised logL1 objective. Appendix C proposes possible applications without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Training still uses NYUv2, VOID, IRS, Hypersim, and Waymo; evaluation still uses ScanNet++ and KITTI-360. Optical flow, segmentation, restoration, stereo, and multi-sensor applications in Appendix C are prospective, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MiDaS, DepthAnything, UniDepth, pretrained and retrained DepthAnyCamera, FoVA-Depth, and finetuning. Newly cited methods in Appendix C are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The reported backbones, eight tokens per layer, 200K training samples, 40K iterations, batch size 16, image resolutions, and RMSE/δ1 metrics are unchanged. The finetuning protocol and supplementary experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the feature-distribution and attention analyses, finetuning and computational-cost comparisons, token-placement and loss ablations, supervised-loss and fisheye-frame controls, and qualitative reconstructions. Appendix C adds discussion rather than new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests for its experiments. The reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain all numerical entries, and the qualitative result figures match. For example, Table 1 retains UniDepth with Calibration Tokens at RMSE/δ1 of 0.244/0.766 on ScanNet++ and 2.040/0.664 on KITTI-360.

T1.justification: The token formulation, camera-transformation equations, training objective in Equations 1–3, and metric definitions in Table 6 are unchanged. Appendix C contains conceptual connections, not new mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and main discussion retain the claims of lightweight adaptation of frozen depth estimators, self-supervised training from perspective images, backward compatibility, and one token set for indoor and outdoor evaluation.

C2.justification: New Appendix C expands the applicability discussion to other perception tasks and explains how camera-induced shift could affect multi-sensor fusion. It also connects backward compatibility to continual learning. These are prospective interpretations; existing result explanations and backbone-dependent limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a second code-access link, Suchisrit/CalibrationTokens, while retaining JungHeeKim29/calibration-token. Hardware, optimizer settings, distortion-parameter ranges, and other implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish what the additional repository contains.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds connections to other perception tasks and continual learning, supported by 29 additional references, including RAFT, SegFormer, and Restormer. This expands the future-application context while retaining the existing depth-estimation, fisheye, and token-method positioning and novelty claims.

P1.justification: v5 adds the short supplementary section C, Discussion, updates the first author's displayed name from Suchisrit to Rit, and expands the code-link text. The existing scientific prose and section sequence are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves between columns on page 7, Figure 6 moves from page 7 to page 8, and surrounding text and tables reflow. References and supplementary pages also shift. All eleven figures and six tables retain their substantive content and display organization.

improvement.justification: Appendix C modestly improves the explanation of broader relevance by connecting camera-induced distribution shift to multi-sensor fusion and backward compatibility to continual learning. These extensions are presented as prospective applications. The contextual gain is limited: the method, experimental evidence, implementation settings, and existing limitations are unchanged.
